topic: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash KV cache compression explained for local runners
title: KV cache compression isn't a flag
description: Working title; the package stage overwrites. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash cuts its KV cache to 890 bytes per token. (Narration is AI-generated.)
hook_candidates: Eight hundred ninety bytes per token.
DeepSeek just made context nearly free.
Your chat memory isn't the model. It's the notes.
One million tokens. One tiny note each.
Four hundred thirty-seven times smaller notes.
Your memory fills. The notes did it.
DeepSeek's cache shrank four hundred thirty-seven times.
Stop blaming the model. Blame its notes.
Eight hundred ninety bytes. A whole context.
The flag isn't the compression. The model is.
Your flag isn't the trick. The training is.
narration_full: Your flag isn't the trick. The training is. DeepSeek's new cache bill: eight hundred ninety bytes per token. The belief: compression is a switch. Set a flag, shrink the KV cache, the running notes kept per token, to four-bit. The truth: DeepSeek trained it into the weights. No switch involved. Layers share one set of notes, each stored four-bit from training. Per-token cache drops about four hundred thirty-seven-fold versus DeepSeek V one. The myth still half works. llama.cpp's cache flags still shrink notes on models you run. On DeepSeek, quantizing the key half of that cache once gave confident gibberish on every backend. Your flag nudges the cache. The training rebuilt it.

analogy.mapping: a runtime cache flag is a switch on the wall; trained-in compression is the building rewired
analogy.limit: the switch still works a little, so the picture must not imply flags do nothing
